name: @telora/mcp-products

tools.name: telora_product
tools.description: Product registry: manage the portfolio of software products. Each product scopes focuses, deliveries, issues, and context documents. Actions: list products, create a new product (name required), get product details (by name or id), update product settings (vision, audience, QA services, QA target), overview (full product summary with focuses and deliveries), QA TARGET: qaTargetEnvironment / qaTargetBaseUrl / qaTargetAccessNote declare where a human goes to test the product's built UI -- one per product. QA packets (telora_product_focus qa_get) write case paths RELATIVE to qaTargetBaseUrl (http/https), so a human can open each case directly; null clears a field. get returns all three. register_local_endpoint (DEPRECATED -- use `telora_local_model create` instead. Retained for back-compat only: it still writes the legacy single per-product local_model_coordinates blob, which the org-scoped `local_models` registry supersedes. Registers non-secret local-model coordinates {baseUrl, model, wireApi} + a per-product engine binding; the API key stays local and is NEVER sent or stored). List responses include a 1-based `index` on each item (response-local; recomputed per call).

id.description: DEPRECATED alias for productId. Product UUID.

name.description: Product name (required for create; optional for get as case-insensitive match)

nexusIntakeRoleId.description: Agent role UUID the daemon's nexus-intake poll assigns to scope accepted cross-product requests (sibling of the accept policy; null clears it -> falls back to the org's Developer role)

towerConcurrencyLimit.description: The product's tower limit: how many of its foci may hold a live coding or review team at once (update). A focus occupies a slot only while it has a live team; armed foci beyond the limit wait, cleared in focus rank order. null clears it (the host session cap alone bounds the product). See docs/runbook-tower.md

qaTargetEnvironment.description: QA target: the name of the environment a human tests this product's built UI in, e.g. 'staging' (update; null clears)

qaTargetBaseUrl.description: QA target base URL (http/https). QA packet case paths are RELATIVE to it -- a base of https://staging.example/app and a path /focuses open https://staging.example/app/focuses (update; null clears)

qaTargetAccessNote.description: QA target access note: how a human gets in -- login, test account, seed data (update; null clears)

qaServices.description: QA environment service URLs (null to clear)

port.description: Port number on the QA host

model.description: Local-model id to pass to the engine (register_local_endpoint)

wireApi.description: Wire API for the local model; defaults to 'responses' (register_local_endpoint)

engine.description: Per-product coding engine binding; defaults to 'codex' (register_local_endpoint)

tools.name: telora_product_delivery
tools.description: Work packages: individual shippable increments within a focus. Each delivery has acceptance criteria, technical context, and tracks progress through issues. Actions: list deliveries (filter by status/focus), create a delivery (name + productId; injectionNodeId anchors the delivery to a reality-tree injection -- REQUIRED when the focus is past planning and has an active reality tree: the create is REFUSED (error, no row) if omitted, and likewise refused on a past-planning focus that has no tree. Anchoring is the default path; for a genuinely tree-less delivery you must pass BOTH allowUnanchored=true AND unanchoredReason (a bare override with no reason is refused). The converse also holds: an injection already materialized by a live delivery REFUSES a second one (duplicate_injection_anchor, no row) -- put residual work on the EXISTING delivery it names, or for a genuinely deliberate split pass BOTH allowDuplicateAnchor=true AND duplicateAnchorReason. each of these two is an effortful, reason-bearing, attributed override, and a bare boolean with no reason is refused (override_reason_required). AIM AT CAUSES: the injection a delivery anchors to targets the CAUSES the delivery changes, never an undesired effect. Write the delivery's acceptance criteria as those causes' declared futures -- what verify judges it on; the undesired effects the causes EARN are the focus's criteria, judged at the focus review once every delivery that earns them has landed, so no delivery is held to a sibling's work. REVIEW-FINDING RULE: no delivery is created in answer to a review finding -- except one that takes a NEW GAP. While a focus holds an OPEN review-filed finding, an agent create on that focus is REFUSED (review_finding_open, no row), naming the findings -- close a shortfall as a Bug or Context Group on the delivery it was filed against. The one admitted create: it names the findings it takes (takesFindingIssueIds), the review RECORDED each as a concern (no not_met criterion names it -- a blocking finding never moves), and it anchors an injection no live delivery holds (the new gap's own cause/effect/injection). The named findings move to the new delivery. New work found after a delivery is done goes HERE, never as a Task on the done delivery (refused). RECORD/QUEUE RULE (an armed focus): the create is never refused for being out of scope. On a focus a human has ARMED, a delivery whose injection serves no effect the arm covers is CREATED and RECORDED -- it rests at execution_status 'planning', is invisible to the running team, and executes when the focus is next armed. The response says so and names the act that would make it run NOW instead: draw a causal edge (sufficient or and) from one of its injection's targets to an effect the arm already covers, which makes it means rather than new intent. Nothing is refused and nothing is frozen; do not re-try the create with different wording; declare workFacing 'outward'|'inward' at create to record whether the delivery opens new ground or refines existing ground), update delivery fields (description, criteria, status), operationalize (attach to org tree), delete, reorder priority (deliveryIds in rank order; the response is the reordered rows ONLY -- the ids given, in their new rank, at `detail` (default summary), with notFoundIds naming any id that is no delivery of the product -- for the surrounding order, call list with a focusId). attribute_commit (deliveryId + commitSha + reason): credit an ALREADY-MERGED commit in the delivery's focus merge batches to this delivery, so verify counts its work. Use it when a commit holds this delivery's work but carries the wrong Telora-Delivery trailer -- typically a daemon exit capture trailered `none` or `unattributed`, which a verify hold names as possibly misattributed. It records who credited it and why; it rewrites no history. Never use it to borrow credit for work that is not this delivery's. shortfall_rule: an OPERATOR ruling that named verify-shortfall nodes on a delivery are met or excused (deliveryId, nodeIds, verdict, rationale; optional escalationId links the escalation it answers). It LOWERS the bar verify holds -- an attributed, rationale-bearing act recorded on the delivery, never taken by the team working that delivery -- and it releases a delivery parked on that shortfall so the next verify pass re-judges it with the ruling honored. It does not close the escalation (resolve it with telora_agent escalation_update, which can carry the ruling itself as shortfallRuling). List responses include a 1-based `index` on each item (response-local; recomputed per call).

productId.description: Product UUID (required for list, create, reorder)

deliveryId.description: Delivery UUID (required for update, operationalize, delete, attribute_commit)

commitSha.description: Full 40-character commit id to credit to the delivery (attribute_commit only)

reason.description: Why this commit is the delivery's work (required for attribute_commit; recorded with the credit)

agentSessionId.description: attribute_commit and shortfall_rule: the agent session recording the act, when known. attribute_commit: must be a session of your organization; the agent credential itself is always recorded. shortfall_rule: a coding or merge session on the delivery's focus is refused.

techContext.description: Technical context: stack, repos, key files, architecture notes

focusId.description: Focus UUID, or the focus's short code like "f3" (the `focusKey` a focus list shows). The code is stored on the focus -- issued once at creation, unique within its product, never changed and never reused -- so it keeps naming the same focus after that focus or any other completes, is cancelled or is reordered. Resolving a code needs productId; a code no focus of the product holds is an error naming it. Links the delivery to that focus (create/update) or filters to it (list); null unlinks (update).

injectionNodeId.description: UUID of an injection node in the focus's reality tree that this delivery materializes. Sets product_deliveries.injection_id atomically. Accepted on create and update; pass null on update to unlink. REQUIRED on create when the focus is past planning and has an active reality tree -- the create is REFUSED (error, no row) otherwise. This is the default path; to override for a genuinely tree-less delivery pass allowUnanchored=true WITH a unanchoredReason. The anchor must also be UNSHARED: naming an injection that already carries a live (non-cancelled) delivery is refused with duplicate_injection_anchor, which names the existing delivery so you can re-scope the residual onto it; unlinking (null) is always permitted and is how an existing double anchor is resolved.

allowUnanchored.description: Effortful, reason-bearing OVERRIDE of the create structural-validity gate -- NOT a frictionless peer to anchoring. The default path is to anchor the delivery to an injection (injectionNodeId); only pass allowUnanchored=true for a genuinely tree-less delivery, and you MUST pass unanchoredReason alongside it. A bare allowUnanchored with no reason is refused (override_reason_required): skipping the differential instrument is a deliberate, recorded act.

unanchoredReason.description: Required when allowUnanchored=true: a non-blank explanation of why this delivery legitimately has no reality-tree anchor. Recorded durably as the override's justification so a silent skip of the differential instrument cannot pass.

allowDuplicateAnchor.description: Effortful, reason-bearing OVERRIDE of the duplicate-anchor gate -- the RARE path, not a frictionless peer. Before reaching for it: if the injection already has a live delivery, the intended move is to put the work on THAT delivery (re-scope the residual onto it with telora_product_issue create, or telora_product_delivery update). Finding an injection's desired effect already partly landed is NOT a reason to abandon the work -- the anchor is what is wrong, not the work. Only pass allowDuplicateAnchor=true when two deliveries genuinely must materialize one injection, and you MUST pass duplicateAnchorReason alongside it. A bare allowDuplicateAnchor with no reason is refused (override_reason_required). Two deliveries on one injection split the evidence for one desired effect: verify partitions commits by the Telora-Delivery trailer, so the sibling ends up holding acceptance criteria it has no trailered commits to evidence.

duplicateAnchorReason.description: Required when allowDuplicateAnchor=true: a non-blank explanation of why this injection legitimately needs a second live delivery. Recorded durably on the delivery with its attribution (who declared the split, and whether by an agent or a human), so a deliberate split is an attributed act rather than a silent second anchor.

takesFindingIssueIds.description: create only: the OPEN review-filed findings (issue ids) this delivery takes onto a NEW gap. Admitted only when the review recorded each as a concern (no not_met criterion names it) and injectionNodeId is an injection no live delivery holds; the findings then move to the new delivery. A blocking finding, or one no review recorded a verdict fact for, is refused and stays where it was filed.

executionStatus.description: Execution status. On create: overrides the focus-stage-aware default ('queued' when the parent focus is past planning, otherwise 'planning'). On update: new status. On list: filter.

workFacing.description: Work-facing novelty label declared at scope time (create) or re-declared on re-scope (update). 'outward' = a capability the user did not have before (new ground; includes machine/tooling capabilities -- the axis is novelty, not product-vs-system). 'inward' = improving a capability that already exists. Declare it as a byproduct of scoping each delivery -- it forces the explicit 'new ground or improving old ground?' question. Read downstream as a mirror of where intent-energy went, never a quota.

parentNodeId.description: Target org unit or stream UUID (operationalize only)

deliveryIds.description: Ordered array of delivery UUIDs for reorder (first = rank 0 = highest priority). The reorder response is these rows only, at `detail`; call list for the surrounding order.

includeIssueCounts.description: Include done/total issue counts per delivery (list only)

nodeIds.description: shortfall_rule only: the reality-tree node ids the verify shortfall names (in this delivery's tree; the park escalation lists them)

verdict.description: shortfall_rule only: met (the desired effect is achieved) or excused (the node no longer binds this delivery); applies to every node in nodeIds

rationale.description: shortfall_rule only (required): why the nodes are met or excused -- recorded with the ruling

escalationId.description: shortfall_rule only: the escalation this ruling answers (must be anchored to the same delivery, or unanchored)

tools.name: telora_product_focus
tools.description: Execution roadmap: group deliveries into themed work scopes. Focuses define what the AI daemon works on -- assigning an agent role queues the focus for autonomous execution. Actions: list focuses for a product, create a focus (name + productId), update focus settings (description, status, agent role, pipeline config), reorder focus priority (focusIds in rank order; the response is the reordered rows ONLY -- the ids given, in their new rank, at `detail` (default summary), with notFoundIds naming any id that is no focus of the product -- for the surrounding order, call list), merges (list merge history for a focus), retrospective_trigger (create a pending retrospective for a focus), retrospective_run (execute a pending retrospective via LLM), retrospective_list (list retrospectives for a focus), retrospective_get (get a single retrospective by ID), review_complete (terminal action for a review agent: writes a focus_reviews row with outcome + summary + references, and updates focus.last_reviewed_at and focus.last_review_outcome. A finding blocks only when a not_met criterion names it (acVerdicts[].issueIds); everything else the review files is recorded as a concern; a not_met reopening a criterion an earlier review under the same arm judged met with evidence blocks only when its acVerdicts[].falsifier test fails at the judged commit; a review whose verdicts cover every criterion with none not_met is recorded as approved), review_list (read completed focus reviews back, newest first, with the decisions taken under uncertainty each one recorded -- question, options, chosen, why reversible, what changes if the human decides otherwise; scope by focusId, productId, or omit both for the whole organization; carries the decision-record rate: the share of completed reviews that recorded at least one resolved fork), review_get (read one focus review by focusReviewId: full summary plus its decisions rendered for a human), criteria_standing (the focus's FLOOR, read without running a review: what this focus is FOR, from BOTH statements of it, and where each part stands. Every entry carries source: 'tree' criteria are the futures (frt_statement) of the undesired effects the focus's ARM covers, each with its nodeId, seq, drafted (a MACHINE wrote that future and a human accepted it by arming) and landing; 'declared' criteria are the lines of the focus's own acceptance_criteria field. THE TWO ARE JUDGED BY DIFFERENT RULES, and status says which fired: a tree criterion reads 'met' ONLY when VERIFY RECORDED its node's future as landed -- reality, read from the node row, never from any text and never from a delivery targeting the node -- while a declared criterion reads 'addressed' when a current delivery DECLARES it. Met and addressed are different claims (reality vs scoping); 'open' is everything else, and every open criterion is echoed verbatim. treeBasis says WHOSE statement of the bar you are reading: armed_stamp (the arm's own armed_baseline_criteria, verbatim -- THE bar, immune to a later frt_statement edit), derived_live_unstamped_arm (armed before the stamp existed, so derived live and APPROXIMATE), derived_live_unarmed, or none. On an UN-ARMED focus the tree half is a PREVIEW of what an arm would stamp and what it would REFUSE on: floorBasis reports derived_live_unarmed -- never a floor, because nothing was stamped to reach -- and the read adds unstatedCoveredEffects (covered effects with NO stated future, which is what the arm refuses on, named by the same seq the refusal message names) and draftedCoveredEffects (covered effects whose future is only a machine draft: stamped, not refused). Consult it before adding another delivery to a focus that may already be close to met, and before arming one. Available BETWEEN reviews and on a focus that has NEVER been reviewed: it is a read, not a review act, so it needs no review session, renders no verdict, and has no 'excused' -- excusing a criterion stays a review act with separation of duties. A focus with NEITHER kind of criterion has NOT reached a floor: floorBasis reports no_criteria_declared, which means the focus has gone unmeasured, not that it has arrived -- the act that produces tree criteria is anchoring deliveries to injections that target CAUSES (each stating its future) and stating the frt_statement on the undesired effects those causes earn. An anchored focus whose covered nodes are ALL entities is scoped, not unscoped: it reports treeBasis derived_live_unarmed with zero judgeable criteria plus armWouldRefuseNoEffect=true -- the arm_criteria_required refusal an arm would raise right now. Both scans are bounded and REPORT their bounds (deliveryScan, treeScan): a truncated node scan errs toward open, but a truncated targets-edge or injection-anchor scan SHRINKS a live-derived bar. The delivery bound does NOT shrink it -- when that bound bites the anchors are re-resolved separately (deliveryScan.anchors / anchorsTruncated) so the tree half stays whole. If any scan DID shorten a live derivation the read says so outright: treeCoverageIncomplete=true and floorBasis derived_live_incomplete, which is neither a reached floor nor a missed one -- criteria may be absent from the list entirely, so do not read a short open list as nearly-done), growth_since_arming (REPORTS how the focus has grown since the operator armed it -- it refuses nothing and gates nothing. One read returns armedDeliveryCount (what the focus HELD at the arm; null when it was never armed), currentDeliveryCount (what it holds now), armedBaselineAt, and additionsSinceArming -- every delivery added since, each NAMING what anchored it: the injection seq + statement, the verbatim unanchored_reason, injection_unresolved (anchored, but this read could not name to what), or no_anchor_recorded. An addition that has since been CANCELLED stays in the list flagged isCancelled -- it was added against the arm and its anchor is part of the history -- while currentDeliveryCount counts only what the focus still HOLDS. Read the top-level basis before trusting the number: ONLY baseline_delivery_ids is EXACT (the id set was stamped at the arm edge). backfilled_delivery_ids is APPROXIMATE -- the baseline was RECONSTRUCTED at baselineRecordedAt from what the focus held then, so growth inside that window is invisible; unverified_delivery_ids is APPROXIMATE -- an id set with no recorded provenance, which cannot be shown to be an arm-instant snapshot; created_at_fallback is APPROXIMATE -- no id set at all, so additions are inferred from creation time. never_armed means there is no arm to measure against -- an empty additions list and a null armed count, never growth from zero). qa_get (a focus's HUMAN QA standing in one read: state -- null (never entered QA), awaiting (its team finished; it waits in its product's QA queue), passed or failed -- with stateAt and who recorded it (recordedBy, recordedByKind); the CURRENT UI test packet (packetId, status pending|ready|failed|no_ui_surface, the reviewedSha it describes, its cases -- each with the criterion, what was built, a path RELATIVE to the product's QA target, click-level steps, the expected result and its recorded result: passed, failed or not_run, null while it has none (recording the verdict records not_run for every case without one) -- casesError when the stored cases are unreadable, failedCaseIds: derived, the cases whose result is failed, and acknowledgement: null unless QA passed was recorded over failed cases, then who accepted which of them and when (failedCaseIds, acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedByKind, acknowledgedAt)); and the product's qaTarget (environment, baseUrl, accessNote). packet is null while awaiting until the packet is written. A case of a packet written after a QA fail may carry priorCaseId (the previous packet's case it carries forward) and priorResult, the result a person recorded for THAT case last cycle -- failed: this case is its retest; passed: previously passed; not_run: nobody ran it, so it needs a run. priorResult is a mark from the previous cycle, never this cycle's result: a previously passed case has result null until one is recorded. After a QA fail the packet and its case results stay readable here, so a scoping session -- in a CLI or a daemon pass -- plans the fix from them), qa_record (records a HUMAN's QA verdict on a focus that is AWAITING QA: qaVerdict passed|failed, plus optional caseResults -- the result the person found per case, case id -> passed|failed|not_run, merged over the results already recorded; every id must be a case of the current packet. Every case still without a result is recorded not_run in the same write as the verdict. PASSING OVER A FAILED CASE IS ACKNOWLEDGED: while any case is resulted failed, a passed verdict whose acknowledgedFailedCaseIds does not name every failed case records NOTHING and returns {recorded: false, warning} naming the failed cases -- a result, not an error. The acknowledgement is the person's: ask them, never supply it yourself. Once it names them all the pass is never refused over them, and is stored with who acknowledged, when, and the failed case ids accepted. failedCaseIds is DEPRECATED (use caseResults): each id is recorded failed. QA is a RECORDED state: it never gates focus or PRD execution, and a pass changes nothing else. FAILED returns a COMPLETE focus to active and, in the same write, stops its arm exactly like an operator stop (role cleared, operator_stopped_at stamped): the focus does NOT resume on its own -- that is final until a human arms it again. Refused (state_conflict) unless the focus is awaiting QA, and on a cancelled focus. Not available to daemon-spawned teams (MCP execution profile): a team never records a human's QA verdict). Every listed focus carries qaState, qaStateAt and qaPacketId (the human QA state -- recorded only, it gates nothing; qaPacketId null while awaiting means the packet is pending); a detail='full' read adds qaRecordedBy, qaRecordedByKind and qaPacket ({packetId, status, reviewedSha, failedCaseIds, caseCount, verdict} -- the current packet in brief; read it whole with qa_get; when the packets could not be read the list says qaPacketsUnread=true and omits qaPacket rather than reporting none). Every listed focus carries armEndedReason (with armEndedAt): WHY the daemon ended its armed run, when it ended one. A focus with assignedAgentRoleId null is un-armed, and that single fact has three different causes -- the focus FINISHED (the lifecycle clear), an operator STOPPED it, or its REVIEW BUDGET was spent (armEndedReason='review_budget_spent': the review loop reached TELORA_REVIEW_CYCLE_CAP without converging, so the daemon released the arm with the criteria still unmet and the findings still open recorded on the focus, and only a NEW arm grants further cycles). Read it before re-arming: a null reason means the focus was not stopped by a spent budget. Full detail (the cycle count, the cap, the unmet criteria, the open blocking findings, and openConcerns -- the open review concerns, each by key and title, recorded for the human and not worked by the arm) rides armEndedDetail on a detail='full' read. On update, pass `clearReviewRequest: true` to clear `product_focuses.review_requested_at` -- the non-SQL recovery path for a focus stuck with a stale review request. List responses include a 1-based `index` on each item (response-local; recomputed per call).

productId.description: Product UUID (required for list, create, reorder; optional scope for review_list, and needed wherever a focus short code like "f3" must be resolved -- including criteria_standing, growth_since_arming, qa_get and qa_record)

focusId.description: Focus UUID, or the focus's short code like "f3" (the `focusKey` a focus list shows). The code is stored on the focus -- issued once at creation, unique within its product, never changed and never reused -- so it keeps naming the same focus after that focus or any other completes, is cancelled or is reordered. Resolving a code needs productId; a code no focus of the product holds is an error naming it. Required for update; also required for review_complete, criteria_standing, growth_since_arming, qa_get and qa_record; optional scope for review_list.

description.description: What this focus aims to achieve

acceptanceCriteria.description: Focus-level (outcome) acceptance criteria: criteria that span the focus and no single delivery can satisfy alone. This is the home for an outcome-level criterion relocated up from a delivery. Enumerated by review_complete alongside each delivery's criteria, so a relocated criterion is verdicted like any other -- never annotated away in a delivery footnote.

status.description: Focus status. On update: sets the focus status. On list: filters to that status, OR name 'open' for the OPEN set -- active + proposed foci that can still absorb new work -- in a single call. On an agent profile, OMITTING status defaults to the open set (scoping reads open intent); a caller wanting terminal foci names 'complete'/'cancelled' explicitly. The human profile omitting status is unchanged (the full history, active and proposed foci first).

readOnly.description: Whether this focus runs in read-only audit mode. Honored on CREATE (an audit-authored focus is read_only=true by construction). The daemon is the sole writer that flips it back to false on ratified release, so passing it on update is a no-op -- it cannot disable audit mode.

assignedAgentRoleId.description: Agent role UUID to assign, or null to unassign (update only). Setting it non-null ARMS the focus -- a human go-signal (unless durably delegated), NOT the tail of scoping: scoping ends at "scoped, un-armed". Arming is a declared, attributed act -- state the activation intent via armNote in the same call (see armNote).

armNote.description: Required when this update ARMS the focus (assignedAgentRoleId set non-null): a non-blank declaration of the activation intent. Arming is a declared, attributed act -- the same standard as the delivery tool's unanchoredReason -- so a bare arm with no stated intent is refused (arm_note_required). Recorded durably as product_focuses.arm_note alongside armed_by/armed_by_kind (who armed it and whether by an agent or a human). It marks and records the act; it does NOT forbid a legitimate agent arm under durable delegation. Not needed to unarm (assignedAgentRoleId=null).

pipelineConfig.description: Pipeline configuration (update only). Auto-review defaults ON; pass review.enabled=false to opt out. Per-pass model selection: `models: { coding, review }` pins the cloud model for each pass (omit a slot to inherit); the legacy focus-wide `model` is read as the coding-pass value when models.coding is absent. Model ids are validated against the registry server-side. Per-pass effort: `efforts: { coding, review }` sets the effort each pass runs at -- one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max; null clears that pass (inherit), an omitted pass is left as stored. Effort precedence: this focus override > the org default (telora_organization set_pass_efforts) > the engine default (no flag). Each engine runs the nearest level it accepts: Codex has no max, so max runs as xhigh. A detail='full' list reports each focus's effectiveEfforts {coding, review}: the level the pass will run at on its engine, its source layer (focus-override | org-default | default), the engine and engineSource (focus-override | local-model | model-implied | org-default | default), and mappedFrom/note when the engine runs a different level than requested. Only a focus engine override or a focus local model makes the engine certain; otherwise an unseen org-authored workflow stage (engine, model, or a stage local model that holds codex even against a focus model) or the daemon host's product default engine may decide it, so the pass also carries byEngine {claude, codex} and an engineNote, and exact=false when the engines would run different levels (the level is then conditional).

focusReviewId.description: Focus review UUID (required for review_get; review_list returns it on each item)

focusIds.description: Ordered array of focus UUIDs for reorder (first = rank 0). The reorder response is these rows only, at `detail`; call list for the surrounding order.

summary.description: Review summary markdown (required for review_complete: the client enforces this even though the server tolerates its absence -- see the reconciliation note in the review_complete dispatch case)

createdIssueIds.description: Issue UUIDs created during the review (review_complete only)

agentSessionId.description: Review agent session UUID (required for review_complete: must be the active review session for the focus)

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the review session started (review_complete only)

decisions.description: Decisions-taken-under-uncertainty records folded into the focus review (review_complete only). Each entry is a fork the machine resolved when it believed a human owned the call: the question, the options considered, what was chosen, why the choice is reversible, and what changes if the human decides otherwise. Rendered as an explicit section in the stored review summary; omit (or pass []) when no such decisions were taken and the section renders explicitly empty.

acVerdicts.description: Per-acceptance-criterion verdicts folded into the focus review. REQUIRED for review_complete when outcome === "approved" AND the focus enumerates acceptance criteria: an approved review must carry one entry per criterion or the server rejects it. THE CRITERIA COME FROM THREE PLACES, and the arm's are the ones most often missed: (1) the TREE criteria the arm STAMPED on the focus (product_focuses.armed_baseline_criteria -- one per undesired effect the arm covers, its stated future), (2) each delivery's acceptance criteria, and (3) the focus-level acceptanceCriteria. Read them with criteria_standing before you review; a criterion you were never shown is still refused. Each entry names the criterion verbatim and a verdict of met / not_met / excused. A verdict on a tree criterion is keyed to its reality-tree node SERVER-SIDE, from the stamp -- do not send a nodeId. ONE ENTRY PER STAMPED EFFECT, NOT PER SENTENCE: two covered effects may state the SAME future, and each is its own criterion owning its own verdict, so repeat the identical criterion string as many times as the tree states it (entries are keyed onto their nodes in the arm's stamped seq order). The refusal names each uncovered tree criterion with its node id, which is what distinguishes them. `not_met` requires a rationale naming the gap and blocks an approved review; name the issue(s) that record the gap in its issueIds. A MET CRITERION REOPENS ONLY ON A DEMONSTRATED FAILURE: when an earlier review under the same arm judged the criterion met with evidence, a not_met blocks only if it names a `falsifier` (a test you committed on the focus branch) that the daemon runs and sees FAIL at the commit that review judged; an argued, undemonstrated reopening is recorded as a concern (never refused). A FINDING BLOCKS ONLY WHEN A not_met CRITERION NAMES IT: an issue listed in a not_met verdict's issueIds is recorded as blocking (it sends its delivery back to coding); every other issue the review files is recorded as a CONCERN -- it stays open but routes nothing. A review whose verdicts cover every criterion with none not_met is recorded as APPROVED whatever outcome you sent. A gaps_found with no not_met verdict is refused while any criterion still lacks a verdict. `met` NAMES WHERE IT IS PROVEN: an approved review is refused (nothing stored, no cycle spent -- resubmit in the same session) while any met lacks `evidence`; prose, commands, globs, absolute or `..` paths are refused. A ref that does not resolve at the judged commit leaves the node for verify to judge. `excused` waives the criterion (lowers a bar) and requires BOTH a non-empty rationale AND reviewSessionId set to your review session id -- the same separation of duties a ratified shortfall requires. An unmet criterion is named, never absorbed into the summary; omit only when the focus has no acceptance criteria.

issueIds.description: not_met verdicts only: the UUIDs of the issues (on this focus) that record the gap this criterion falsifies. These -- and only these -- are the review's BLOCKING findings. Refused on met/excused.

evidence.description: met verdicts only (refused on not_met/excused): 1-5 repository-relative references where the criterion is proven -- `path`, `path::test name` or `path:LINE`. REQUIRED on every met in an approved review. Prefer the test that would fail if the criterion were false.

falsifier.description: not_met verdicts only (refused on met/excused): the test that DEMONSTRATES the failure -- a repository-relative test file you COMMITTED on the focus branch (testPath), optionally one test in it (testName). REQUIRED for a not_met to block when an earlier review under the SAME arm judged the criterion met with evidence (a reopening): the daemon runs it at the commit that review judged, and the verdict's issueIds block only when it FAILS there. Absent, unresolvable or passing, the issues are recorded as concerns and the review record says why. Ignored on a first-time not_met.

clearReviewRequest.description: If true, clears product_focuses.review_requested_at (update only). Use to unstick a focus whose review_requested_at is set but no review will run.

qaVerdict.description: The human's QA verdict (required for qa_record): passed or failed. Recording it records not_run for every case of the packet still without a result. passed while any case is resulted failed needs acknowledgedFailedCaseIds. failed returns a complete focus to active and stops its arm like an operator stop -- it does not resume until a human arms it again. QA never gates execution.

caseResults.description: qa_record only: the result the person found for each case of the current QA packet -- an object, case id (cases[].id from qa_get) -> passed, failed or not_run. Merged over the results already recorded: a case not named keeps its result. Every id must be a case of the current packet. Every case still without a result is recorded not_run in the same write as the verdict.

acknowledgedFailedCaseIds.description: qa_record only: the PERSON's acknowledgement that QA passes over failed cases -- the id of every case resulted failed, the ones this call's caseResults marks failed included. Needed when qaVerdict is passed and any case is failed: without it, or naming fewer than all of them, nothing is recorded and the result is {recorded: false, warning} naming the failed cases. Ask the person; never supply it on your own. With it the pass is never refused over those cases, and is stored with who acknowledged, when, and the ids accepted.

failedCaseIds.description: DEPRECATED: use caseResults. qa_record only: each id is recorded failed, as caseResults would record it -- it no longer replaces the results already recorded. Every id must be a case of the current packet.

ratify.description: If true, RATIFIES this focus's remediation plan: stamps product_focuses.ratified_at=now (update only). On a read-only audit focus this is the human gate signal -- the daemon then performs the sole planning->execution crossing (flips read_only=false and releases held planning deliveries to queued). Distinct from readOnly: the human sets ratified_at; the daemon flips read_only.

tools.name: telora_product_strategy
tools.description: DEPRECATED: use telora_product_focus. This alias accepts both legacy strategyId/strategyIds and new focusId/focusIds parameters and will be removed in a future release.

productId.description: Product UUID (required for list, create, reorder; optional scope for review_list, and needed wherever a focus short code like "f3" must be resolved -- including criteria_standing, growth_since_arming, qa_get and qa_record)

focusId.description: Focus UUID, or the focus's short code like "f3" (the `focusKey` a focus list shows). The code is stored on the focus -- issued once at creation, unique within its product, never changed and never reused -- so it keeps naming the same focus after that focus or any other completes, is cancelled or is reordered. Resolving a code needs productId; a code no focus of the product holds is an error naming it. Required for update; also required for review_complete, criteria_standing, growth_since_arming, qa_get and qa_record; optional scope for review_list.

description.description: What this focus aims to achieve

acceptanceCriteria.description: Focus-level (outcome) acceptance criteria: criteria that span the focus and no single delivery can satisfy alone. This is the home for an outcome-level criterion relocated up from a delivery. Enumerated by review_complete alongside each delivery's criteria, so a relocated criterion is verdicted like any other -- never annotated away in a delivery footnote.

status.description: Focus status. On update: sets the focus status. On list: filters to that status, OR name 'open' for the OPEN set -- active + proposed foci that can still absorb new work -- in a single call. On an agent profile, OMITTING status defaults to the open set (scoping reads open intent); a caller wanting terminal foci names 'complete'/'cancelled' explicitly. The human profile omitting status is unchanged (the full history, active and proposed foci first).

readOnly.description: Whether this focus runs in read-only audit mode. Honored on CREATE (an audit-authored focus is read_only=true by construction). The daemon is the sole writer that flips it back to false on ratified release, so passing it on update is a no-op -- it cannot disable audit mode.

assignedAgentRoleId.description: Agent role UUID to assign, or null to unassign (update only). Setting it non-null ARMS the focus -- a human go-signal (unless durably delegated), NOT the tail of scoping: scoping ends at "scoped, un-armed". Arming is a declared, attributed act -- state the activation intent via armNote in the same call (see armNote).

armNote.description: Required when this update ARMS the focus (assignedAgentRoleId set non-null): a non-blank declaration of the activation intent. Arming is a declared, attributed act -- the same standard as the delivery tool's unanchoredReason -- so a bare arm with no stated intent is refused (arm_note_required). Recorded durably as product_focuses.arm_note alongside armed_by/armed_by_kind (who armed it and whether by an agent or a human). It marks and records the act; it does NOT forbid a legitimate agent arm under durable delegation. Not needed to unarm (assignedAgentRoleId=null).

pipelineConfig.description: Pipeline configuration (update only). Auto-review defaults ON; pass review.enabled=false to opt out. Per-pass model selection: `models: { coding, review }` pins the cloud model for each pass (omit a slot to inherit); the legacy focus-wide `model` is read as the coding-pass value when models.coding is absent. Model ids are validated against the registry server-side. Per-pass effort: `efforts: { coding, review }` sets the effort each pass runs at -- one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max; null clears that pass (inherit), an omitted pass is left as stored. Effort precedence: this focus override > the org default (telora_organization set_pass_efforts) > the engine default (no flag). Each engine runs the nearest level it accepts: Codex has no max, so max runs as xhigh. A detail='full' list reports each focus's effectiveEfforts {coding, review}: the level the pass will run at on its engine, its source layer (focus-override | org-default | default), the engine and engineSource (focus-override | local-model | model-implied | org-default | default), and mappedFrom/note when the engine runs a different level than requested. Only a focus engine override or a focus local model makes the engine certain; otherwise an unseen org-authored workflow stage (engine, model, or a stage local model that holds codex even against a focus model) or the daemon host's product default engine may decide it, so the pass also carries byEngine {claude, codex} and an engineNote, and exact=false when the engines would run different levels (the level is then conditional).

focusReviewId.description: Focus review UUID (required for review_get; review_list returns it on each item)

focusIds.description: Ordered array of focus UUIDs for reorder (first = rank 0). The reorder response is these rows only, at `detail`; call list for the surrounding order.

summary.description: Review summary markdown (required for review_complete: the client enforces this even though the server tolerates its absence -- see the reconciliation note in the review_complete dispatch case)

createdIssueIds.description: Issue UUIDs created during the review (review_complete only)

agentSessionId.description: Review agent session UUID (required for review_complete: must be the active review session for the focus)

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the review session started (review_complete only)

decisions.description: Decisions-taken-under-uncertainty records folded into the focus review (review_complete only). Each entry is a fork the machine resolved when it believed a human owned the call: the question, the options considered, what was chosen, why the choice is reversible, and what changes if the human decides otherwise. Rendered as an explicit section in the stored review summary; omit (or pass []) when no such decisions were taken and the section renders explicitly empty.

acVerdicts.description: Per-acceptance-criterion verdicts folded into the focus review. REQUIRED for review_complete when outcome === "approved" AND the focus enumerates acceptance criteria: an approved review must carry one entry per criterion or the server rejects it. THE CRITERIA COME FROM THREE PLACES, and the arm's are the ones most often missed: (1) the TREE criteria the arm STAMPED on the focus (product_focuses.armed_baseline_criteria -- one per undesired effect the arm covers, its stated future), (2) each delivery's acceptance criteria, and (3) the focus-level acceptanceCriteria. Read them with criteria_standing before you review; a criterion you were never shown is still refused. Each entry names the criterion verbatim and a verdict of met / not_met / excused. A verdict on a tree criterion is keyed to its reality-tree node SERVER-SIDE, from the stamp -- do not send a nodeId. ONE ENTRY PER STAMPED EFFECT, NOT PER SENTENCE: two covered effects may state the SAME future, and each is its own criterion owning its own verdict, so repeat the identical criterion string as many times as the tree states it (entries are keyed onto their nodes in the arm's stamped seq order). The refusal names each uncovered tree criterion with its node id, which is what distinguishes them. `not_met` requires a rationale naming the gap and blocks an approved review; name the issue(s) that record the gap in its issueIds. A MET CRITERION REOPENS ONLY ON A DEMONSTRATED FAILURE: when an earlier review under the same arm judged the criterion met with evidence, a not_met blocks only if it names a `falsifier` (a test you committed on the focus branch) that the daemon runs and sees FAIL at the commit that review judged; an argued, undemonstrated reopening is recorded as a concern (never refused). A FINDING BLOCKS ONLY WHEN A not_met CRITERION NAMES IT: an issue listed in a not_met verdict's issueIds is recorded as blocking (it sends its delivery back to coding); every other issue the review files is recorded as a CONCERN -- it stays open but routes nothing. A review whose verdicts cover every criterion with none not_met is recorded as APPROVED whatever outcome you sent. A gaps_found with no not_met verdict is refused while any criterion still lacks a verdict. `met` NAMES WHERE IT IS PROVEN: an approved review is refused (nothing stored, no cycle spent -- resubmit in the same session) while any met lacks `evidence`; prose, commands, globs, absolute or `..` paths are refused. A ref that does not resolve at the judged commit leaves the node for verify to judge. `excused` waives the criterion (lowers a bar) and requires BOTH a non-empty rationale AND reviewSessionId set to your review session id -- the same separation of duties a ratified shortfall requires. An unmet criterion is named, never absorbed into the summary; omit only when the focus has no acceptance criteria.

evidence.description: met verdicts only (refused on not_met/excused): 1-5 repository-relative references where the criterion is proven -- `path`, `path::test name` or `path:LINE`. REQUIRED on every met in an approved review. Prefer the test that would fail if the criterion were false.

falsifier.description: not_met verdicts only (refused on met/excused): the test that DEMONSTRATES the failure -- a repository-relative test file you COMMITTED on the focus branch (testPath), optionally one test in it (testName). REQUIRED for a not_met to block when an earlier review under the SAME arm judged the criterion met with evidence (a reopening): the daemon runs it at the commit that review judged, and the verdict's issueIds block only when it FAILS there. Absent, unresolvable or passing, the issues are recorded as concerns and the review record says why. Ignored on a first-time not_met.

Every case still without a result is recorded not_run in the same write as the verdict.

strategyId.description: DEPRECATED: use focusId. Focus UUID (required for update)

strategyIds.description: DEPRECATED: use focusIds. Ordered array of focus UUIDs for reorder

tools.name: telora_product_focus_debug
tools.description: WRITES agent-authored, human-facing visualizations on request (the focus Debug tab) -- it is NOT the canonical store of current architectural reality. To READ current reality during scoping, use telora_reality_tree get/dump (and telora_reality_tree_node/_edge list), not this tool. Focus debug artifacts: agent-written code-reality views (Mermaid graph + markdown panels) rendered on the focus page Debug tab. One row per (focusId, sectionKind). Section kinds: mermaid, file_inventory, git_stats, test_status, lint_typecheck, ac_verification. (Two sections are DAEMON-written and absent from this enum -- do not author or clear either: integration_sync, the focus branch conflicts with integration; and directive_undelivered, a stage directive its target session ended mid-delivery never received.) Actions: get(focusId) returns all sections + updatedAt; set(focusId, sectionKind, content) upserts one section; clear(focusId, sectionKind?) deletes one section (sectionKind given) or all (omitted).

sectionKind.description: Section kind (required for set; optional for clear -- omit to clear all sections)

content.description: Markdown or Mermaid source (required for set)

agentSessionId.description: Optional agent session UUID to stamp on the row (updated_by_session_id)

tools.name: telora_product_issue
tools.description: Task tracking: manage issues (tasks, bugs, context groups) within deliveries. Issues flow through To Do -> In Progress -> Done. Context groups organize related tasks with shared files and AI context. Actions: list issues (by delivery or product-wide), create an issue (title + deliveryId), update issue fields (status, priority, description), delete an issue. List responses include a 1-based `index` on each item (response-local; recomputed per call).

deliveryId.description: Delivery UUID (required for create; optional filter for list)

productId.description: Product UUID (list: fetch issues across all deliveries)

status.description: Issue status (create default: 'To Do'; list: filter). 'Verified' means confirmed-addressed by a review agent — treated as terminal for delivery completion.

parentIssueId.description: Parent issue UUID (for nesting under context groups)

context.description: Rich text/markdown context for AI agents (Context Group only)

relevantFiles.description: File paths/glob patterns, one per line (Context Group only)

dependsOn.description: Issue UUIDs this context group depends on (CG-level DAG)

falsifiedEffectNodeIds.description: create only, a Bug on a DONE delivery: the met effects (desired_effect reality-tree node ids) its finding shows are FALSE -- verify was wrong about them. Filing the Bug demotes each back to undesired_effect with its stated future (frtStatement) KEPT, attributed to you, so the delivery's own verified injection covers it again at the next arm, and reopens the delivery as verify_failed. Each must be an active desired effect this delivery's injection earned (targeted, or downstream of a target along sufficient/and) that states a future; any other is refused, nothing filed. WORK FOUND AFTER DONE GOES WHERE THE TREE SAYS: a Task on a done delivery is REFUSED -- new work is a new gap: draw its cause, effect and injection and create a NEW delivery in the same focus (telora_product_delivery create, takesFindingIssueIds to move review findings onto it).

completionArtifacts.description: What Done / In Review work produced. files and tests are repository-relative PATHS (e.g. src/foo.ts, src/foo.test.ts) that drift detection probes on disk -- never commands or results such as 'npm run typecheck' or 'build passed'; a non-path entry is stored as a verification note, not an artifact.

tools.name: telora_infra_environment
tools.description: Infrastructure environments: named deployment targets (production, staging, dev) within a product. Each environment groups infrastructure assets and has a status (active, provisioning, decommissioned). usersUrl is the address this environment's USERS open (absolute https): release notes build their links on it, and a human cuts each release (telora_release) for one environment. When usersUrl is unset, the product's QA target base URL counts only for the environment the QA target names. Actions: list (by product), create (name required, unique per product), update, delete. List responses include a 1-based `index` on each item (response-local; recomputed per call).

name.description: Environment name (required for create, unique per product)

usersUrl.description: The address this environment's users open (absolute https); release notes build their links on it (create, update; null clears)

tools.name: telora_infra_asset
tools.description: Infrastructure assets: typed resources (database, container, service, dashboard, storage, proxy, dns, monitoring, ci_cd) within a product. Assets can optionally belong to an environment and store connection details (url, ip, port). Actions: list (by product, optional environment/type filter), create, update, delete. List responses include a 1-based `index` on each item (response-local; recomputed per call).

environmentId.description: Environment UUID (filter for list, assignment for create/update)

assetType.description: Asset type (required for create, filter for list)

dashboardPinned.description: Pin asset link to dashboard product dropdown (requires url)

tools.name: telora_infra_relationship
tools.description: Asset relationships: directed links between infrastructure assets within the same product. Types: connects_to, deploys_to, proxies, depends_on, hosts. Actions: list (by product), create (source + target + type), delete. List responses include a 1-based `index` on each item (response-local; recomputed per call).

tools.name: telora_infra_secret
tools.description: Infrastructure secrets: encrypted key-value pairs stored per asset using Vault. List and create show names only (no values). Use get to decrypt and reveal a secret value on demand. Actions: list (by asset), create (name + value), get (decrypts), delete. List responses include a 1-based `index` on each item (response-local; recomputed per call).

name.description: Secret name (required for create, unique per asset)

secretValue.description: Secret value to encrypt and store (required for create)

tools.name: telora_context_assemble
tools.description: Assemble layered context for a product, focus, or delivery. Returns pre-formatted markdown with product overview, focus/delivery scaffolding, a wiki section drawn from wiki_search using scope-derived queries (or your own `queries` override), and an 'Actions on this <scope>' section enumerating the primary MCP tool + HTTP fallback for each capability available on the entity. Pass an `assembly` recipe to select/compose specific sections over the DB-backed resolver subset, or `modelContextTokens` to lift the wiki budget to your model's context window. Use at session start for architectural/design work.

deliveryId.description: Delivery UUID (adds tech context + acceptance criteria + issues)

queries.description: Override the scope-derived wiki retrieval queries

assembly.description: Optional recipe: ordered source refs over the DB-backed subset (scaffold sections + wiki refs), e.g. ["delivery.acceptance_criteria", "wiki.search(query=\"testing\")"]. Omitted -> the full default recipe. Execution-only refs (git.diff_against_base, worktree, persona, guards) are rejected.

modelContextTokens.description: Your model's context window in tokens (e.g. 200000). Lifts the wiki-retrieval ceiling above the small-context per-scope default; the intent scaffold is uncapped regardless.

tools.name: telora_connector_start
tools.description: Daemon automation: generate configuration and launch the Telora daemon for autonomous agent execution. Creates daemon.json with API credentials and engine settings, then starts the background process.

productId.description: Product UUID to scope this daemon to. Required when the organization has multiple products. Auto-detected when there is only one product.

tools.name: telora_session_state
tools.description: Session bootstrap: returns Telora connection state in a single payload (connected URL, organization, product, active focus + role, pending delivery counts). activeFocus also carries an operator-stop indicator (held: true + operatorStoppedAt timestamp) so a stop is confirmable without reading the daemon log. Used by the SessionStart hook to surface state at chat open. Optional productId; auto-resolved when the organization has a single product. NOTE: branch state (commits ahead of integration) is NOT included in this response -- the server has no git access. For branch state, run `telora-daemon session-state --json` in the repo root.

productId.description: Product UUID. Optional when the organization has only one product.

tools.name: telora_organization
tools.description: Organization settings: the org's per-pass DEFAULT models and efforts (coding, review). Models: the model a focus pass runs when the focus pins none. The harness equivalent of the dashboard's Settings > Default Pass Models pickers, and it accepts exactly what they save: a selectable hosted model id (claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5-5, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna), or an empty string to clear (inherit). Legacy ids that are no longer selectable (e.g. gpt-5-codex, gpt-5, o3-mini, claude-fable-5) are refused; an org already pinned to one still reads it back. Model precedence: a focus pin > an org-authored workflow stage model > this org default > the builtin workflow stage model. Engine: the daemon runs a model on the engine it implies (claude-* on Claude Code, gpt-* on Codex) when the model's layer outranks the pass's engine choice, on one ladder: focus > org-authored workflow stage > org default > product default engine (daemon.json on the daemon host) > builtin workflow stage > global default. So an org default gpt-* model runs on Codex even when the org or product default engine is Claude Code (and an org default claude-* model runs on Claude Code on a Codex-harness product), but a focus engine override or an org-authored stage engine outranks it; a model the chosen engine cannot run is dropped and that engine runs its own default. Per-pass DEFAULT effort (coding, review): one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or an empty string / null to clear (engine default -- no effort flag). Effort precedence: a focus's pipelineConfig.efforts > this org default > the engine default. Each engine runs the nearest level it accepts: Codex has no max, so max runs as xhigh. Actions: get_pass_models (read the current defaults -- models AND efforts), set_pass_models (write models; only the passes you provide change; an empty string clears -> inherit), set_pass_efforts (write efforts via codingEffort/reviewEffort; only the passes you provide change; an empty string or null clears -> engine default).

codingModel.description: Coding-pass default model id (set_pass_models): a selectable Claude or OpenAI hosted id. Empty string clears (inherit); omit to leave unchanged.

reviewModel.description: Review-pass default model id (set_pass_models): a selectable Claude or OpenAI hosted id. Empty string clears (inherit); omit to leave unchanged.

codingEffort.description: Coding-pass default effort (set_pass_efforts): one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Empty string or null clears (engine default); omit to leave unchanged.

reviewEffort.description: Review-pass default effort (set_pass_efforts): one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Empty string or null clears (engine default); omit to leave unchanged.
